es: Leer un resumen académico (abstract) e identificar su objetivo, su método y su conclusión cautelosa, apoyándote en las señales de cada parte y detectando las limitaciones que el texto da a entender.

teaching.en: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.
teaching.es: Un resumen académico es una síntesis breve de un estudio y suele seguir el orden objetivo, método, resultados y conclusión, a menudo en menos de doscientas palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: El abstract condensa todo el estudio: reconocer su orden te permite localizar cada dato.
segments: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the
order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.
teaching.audioText: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.

teaching.en: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.
teaching.es: El objetivo de este estudio es examinar si el sueño afecta al rendimiento en los exámenes, en lugar de limitarse a describir cuánto duermen los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: The aim of this study is to + verbo base. Examine whether plantea una pregunta; rather than la contrasta con lo que el estudio no hace.
segments: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects
exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.
teaching.audioText: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.

teaching.en: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18, who were placed randomly in one of two groups.
teaching.es: La muestra incluyó a 120 participantes de entre 16 y 18 años, que fueron colocados al azar en uno de dos grupos.
teaching.explanationEs: Sample es el grupo estudiado; participants son las personas. Randomly evita que los grupos se formen a propósito.
segments: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18,
who were placed randomly in one of two groups.
teaching.audioText: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18, who were placed randomly in one of two groups.

teaching.en: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.
teaching.es: El método fue sencillo: un grupo siguió un horario de sueño estricto durante dos semanas, mientras que el grupo de control mantuvo sus hábitos habituales.
teaching.explanationEs: El control group sirve de comparación: sin él no se sabe si el cambio se debe al tratamiento.
segments: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule
for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.
teaching.audioText: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.

teaching.en: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests, although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.
teaching.es: Los participantes que durmieron más lograron una puntuación más alta en las pruebas de memoria, aunque la diferencia fue pequeña y varió de un individuo a otro.
teaching.explanationEs: Los resultados se dan con datos (higher score) y a menudo con una reserva (although…).
segments: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests,
although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.
teaching.audioText: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests, although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.

teaching.en: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, but they stress that a correlation between sleep and scores does not prove that one causes the other.
teaching.es: Los autores concluyen que dormir más podría mejorar el rendimiento, pero subrayan que una correlación entre sueño y notas no prueba que una cosa cause la otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Conclude that + may: conclusión cautelosa. Correlación no es causa: una relación estadística no prueba una causa.
segments: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, but they stress that a
correlation between sleep and scores does not prove that one causes the other.

prompt.es: Lee el resumen. ¿Qué parte es la segunda frase?

choices.text: Aim: it says what question the study wants to answer here.
Conclusion: it says what the authors think the results mean.
Method: it says who took part and how they were grouped.

feedback.es: La segunda frase describe quién participó (sesenta adultos) y cómo se agruparon: es el método; la primera frase expone el objetivo.

hint.es: Fíjate en si la frase dice a quién se estudió y cómo, o qué se quiere saber.

origin.text: This study examines whether a daily twenty-minute walk improves concentration. Sixty adults were placed in a walking group or a control group for four weeks.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo de este estudio es examinar cómo afecta el sueño al rendimiento.»

feedback.es: The aim of this study is to + verbo base es la señal que abre el objetivo de un resumen.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que, con of this study, introduce el objetivo.

origin.text: Sleep and memory are often linked in popular articles. The ___ of this study is to examine how sleep affects exam performance.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada grupo siguió un plan de sueño distinto durante dos semanas.»

answer.text: Each group followed a different sleep plan for two weeks

feedback.es: Esta frase describe el método: qué hizo cada grupo y durante cuánto tiempo.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto each group y deja la duración para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen y elige cuál es el método del estudio.

choices.text: Office workers were split by chance into a walking group and a control group.
Office workers were interviewed about their concentration before a holiday.
All eighty office workers walked daily for six weeks and then took a test.

feedback.es: El método describe cómo se formaron los grupos (por azar, uno que camina y otro de control); no hubo entrevistas ni caminó toda la muestra.

origin.audio: This study examines whether a short daily walk improves concentration at work. The sample included eighty office workers, who were placed by chance in a walking group or a control group for six weeks. Workers in the walking group scored higher in an attention test, although the difference between the groups was small. The authors conclude that walking may help concentration, but they add that a longer study is needed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del resumen con la parte que cumple.

pairs: The aim of this study is to examine sleep and stress.
The sample included 200 adults aged 20 to 35.
Participants who slept longer scored higher.
The authors conclude that sleep may reduce stress.

feedback.es: El aim marca el objetivo; the sample included describe la muestra (método); scored higher es un resultado y conclude that… may es una conclusión cautelosa.

pairs: The aim of this study is to examine sleep and stress.
The sample included 200 adults aged 20 to 35.
Participants who slept longer scored higher.
The authors conclude that sleep may reduce stress.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué advierten los autores sobre la correlación?

choices.text: That the students who slept more were the best students in their school.
That a link between two things does not show that one causes the other.
That sleeping more is the most effective way of studying for exams.

feedback.es: Los autores añaden que quienes duermen más quizá también estudian con más regularidad: la correlación puede tener otra causa, no prueba que el sueño mejore las notas.

origin.text: The study found a correlation between hours of sleep and exam scores: students who slept more scored higher. The authors note, however, that students who sleep more may also study more regularly.

prompt.es: Según el resumen, ¿cuál es el método del estudio?

choices.text: Participants chose the time of day that suited them and then described how well they remembered.
Participants studied different material in the morning and were tested later on the same day.
Participants studied the same material at different times and took a test a week later.

feedback.es: El método dice que todos estudiaron el mismo material, unos por la mañana y otros por la tarde, y que la prueba fue una semana después.

origin.text: Many students study late at night. This study aims to examine whether the time of day affects memory performance. The sample included 90 participants aged 17 to 19, who studied the same material either in the morning or in the evening and were tested one week later. Participants who studied in the morning scored slightly higher. The authors conclude that morning study may offer a small advantage, although the differences between participants were large and the results should be read with caution.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la última frase del resumen?

choices.text: That the morning advantage is real but small, and not the same for everyone.
That the morning advantage is large and will apply to every student.
That the morning advantage has been shown to be wrong by the authors' own data.

feedback.es: «May offer a small advantage» y «the differences between participants were large» indican una ventaja real pero pequeña y desigual entre personas; hay que leer los resultados con cautela.

origin.text: Many students study late at night. This study aims to examine whether the time of day affects memory performance. The sample included 90 participants aged 17 to 19, who studied the same material either in the morning or in the evening and were tested one week later. Participants who studied in the morning scored slightly higher. The authors conclude that morning study may offer a small advantage, although the differences between participants were large and the results should be read with caution.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los participantes fueron asignados al azar a uno de dos grupos.»

feedback.es: Randomly indica que los grupos se forman por azar, lo que los hace comparables entre sí.

origin.text: Fifty participants were assigned ___ to one of two groups, so that the groups were as similar as possible.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Qué duda plantea el presentador sobre el estudio?

choices.text: Whether 120 teenagers is enough people to carry out such a study.
Whether the higher scores came from sleep or from the students themselves.
Whether an extra hour of sleep is possible for most teenagers.

feedback.es: El presentador duda porque el resumen no aclara si los participantes ya eran buenos estudiantes: las notas podrían deberse a ellos y no al sueño.

origin.audio: Listeners, today's paper is an abstract I found on memory and sleep. The authors examine 120 teenagers and conclude that an extra hour of sleep may improve test scores, but only slightly. Personally, I would not change my routine yet, because the abstract does not say whether the participants were already good students.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte típica de un resumen falta en este texto?

choices.text: A description of how many people took part in it.
A cautious conclusion about what the results mean.
A clear statement of the aim of the study.

feedback.es: El texto da la muestra (300 trabajadores), un resultado y una conclusión cautelosa (suggest), pero no dice qué pregunta pretendía responder el estudio.

origin.text: This paper reports a survey of 300 workers. Most of them said that they felt better at work after a walk at midday. The authors suggest that bosses could encourage short walks during the working day.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Qué implica la limitación que reconocen los autores?

choices.text: The findings may not apply to people who are less interested.
The findings cannot be trusted, because volunteers often give false answers.
The findings prove that students are more interested than other people.

feedback.es: Una muestra de voluntarios, casi todos universitarios, quizá más interesados en el tema, limita a quién pueden aplicarse los resultados.

origin.audio: In the abstract, the sample is described as two hundred volunteers, most of them students at college. The authors admit that this limits the results, because volunteers may be more interested in the subject than other people.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los autores concluyen que dormir más podría mejorar el rendimiento.»

feedback.es: The authors conclude that… es la señal que introduce la conclusión del resumen, aquí matizada con may.

origin.text: After comparing the two groups, the authors ___ that more sleep may improve performance, although more research is needed.
